stimulus.description: A satellite of mass $m=1000\text{ kg}$ moves in a circular orbit of radius $8.00\times10^{6}\text{ m}$ around Earth, measured from the center of Earth. parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A student claims that when the satellite moves to the larger orbit its kinetic energy decreases but its total mechanical energy increases. Do you agree or disagree with the claim? Justify your answer using the expressions for the energies of a circular orbit.
parts.model_answer: Agree. For a circular orbit $K=GMm/(2r)$ decreases as $r$ increases, while $E=K+U=-GMm/(2r)$ is negative and becomes less negative (increases) as $r$ increases.

rubric_rows.criterion: Agrees with the claim
common_errors: disagrees because a higher orbit has more energy in every form

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the decrease of the kinetic energy with $K=GMm/(2r)$ from the centripetal condition
common_errors: says the kinetic energy increases with the height

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies the increase of the total energy with $E=-GMm/(2r)$, which becomes less negative as $r$ increases
common_errors: says the total energy is positive

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the total mechanical energy of the satellite in a circular orbit of radius $r$, and calculate, in gigajoules (GJ), the change in the total mechanical energy when the satellite moves from $r_1$ to $r_2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the gravitational force equal to the centripetal force to get $K=GMm/(2r)$
required_elements: G M m / r^2 = m v^2 / r
common_errors: uses K = G M m / r

rubric_rows.criterion: Adds the potential energy $U=-GMm/r$ to obtain $E=-GMm/(2r)$
required_elements: E = K + U = - G M m / (2 r)
common_errors: obtains $E=+GMm/(2r)$

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $\Delta E=\tfrac12GMm(1/r_1-1/r_2)$ of about 12.5 with units of gigajoules (positive)
common_errors: gives a negative change

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict the ratio of the orbital speed in the larger orbit to the orbital speed in the original orbit, and justify your answer.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the speed ratio is about 0.707 (the speed decreases)
common_errors: states that the speed increases
states a ratio of 0.500

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies with $v=\sqrt{GM/r}$, so the speed is inversely proportional to the square root of the radius
common_errors: argues only that the satellite is farther away
